body:
_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

Removing version: 1.1 (automated comment)

_Original comment by_ **Scott Stanton (BitBucket: [scott_stanton_veeva](http://bitbucket.org/scott_stanton_veeva))**:

---

This is very annoying if you are using the Google AppEngine ndb decorators like ndb.transactional().  The decorator is generated by @utils.decorator which converts a function to a decorator.   E1120 ends up thinking the decorator arguments are required, so every use of @transactional() generates an error.

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

Yeah, ideally this would have been fixed a long time ago. There are many issues and not enough manpower to provide a fix in time for all of them. The only promise I can make right now is that I'll try to target this for fixing in 1.6, since 1.5 is almost ready for launching.

Comments moved here from #207.

---

Here is a minimal example to reproduce the issue:

```py
def helper(fun):
    def wrapper(b):
        return fun('helper', b)
    return wrapper

@helper
def simple(a, b):
    print a, b

simple('test')
```

> E: 10, 0: No value for argument 'b' in function call (no-value-for-parameter)

---

Here is the same example with the decorator replaced with method composition:

```py
def helper(fun):
    def wrapper(b):
        return fun('helper', b)
    return wrapper

def hard(a, b):
    print a, b

simple = helper(hard)

simple('test')
```

> No errors

---

To prove that pylint is not simply skipping the signature checking for method composition:

```py
def helper(fun):
    def wrapper(b):
        return fun('helper', b)
    return wrapper

def hard(a, b):
    print a, b

simple = helper(hard)

simple('helper?', 'test')
```

> E: 11, 0: Too many positional arguments for function call (too-many-function-args)

---

The issue is not that pylint is incapable of inferring the signature of generated methods, but rather that pylint lacks the instruction to treat decorators as the composed functions they are.

---

This issue seems to stem from the core AST module leaving it up to the consumer to resolve the signature produced by applying the `decorator_list`.

It should be sufficient to detect when a function node has decorators and substitute it with the return value(s?) of the first decorator.

I think it would be generally useful to determine the resulting signature in asteroid. Maybe an attribute like `external_args`?

issue.title: False positive: no-value-for-parameter when called decorator is itself decorated

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
Originally reported by: **BitBucket: [nathanielmanista](http://bitbucket.org/nathanielmanista)**

---

On line 29 of the attached reproduction example, it's nice that pylint tries to determine that the expression in the decorator is a legitimate function call, but it should abort its analysis when it looks up the function being called and sees that that function is itself decorated (and thus its overall type is probably not known or at least very hard to reason about).

This is happening in pylint 1.0.0 and pylint 1.1.0.

The real-world source of this report is in the Melange project (http://code.google.com/p/soc) at a place where we use the App Engine Datastore's NDB API's ndb.transactional decorator with an argument of "xg=True" - ndb.transactional is a decorator that is itself decorated in a way that seems beyond pylint's reasoning. This defect likely affects all users of the App Engine Datastore's NDB API.

This issue was previously reported over at https://bitbucket.org/logilab/pylint.org/issue/6.

---
- Bitbucket: https://bitbucket.org/logilab/pylint/issue/207

issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce
```
import toolz as tz

@tz.curry
def add(x, y):
    return x+y

add(1)(2)

def add2(x, y):
    return x+y
```

issue.title: false E0632 in case of special decorated functions

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce
```
from functools import wraps


def example_decorator(func):
    """ ... """
    @wraps(func)
    def _wrapper_fn(*args, **kw):
        (param, incremented, message) = func(*args, **kw)
        print(message)
        return (param, incremented)
    return _wrapper_fn


@example_decorator
def example_function(aaa):
    """ ... """
    return (aaa, aaa+1, "here is a message")


(VALUE, INCREMENTED) = example_function(10)

```

### Current behavior
It marks the return value of the function with E0632: Possible unbalanced tuple unpacking...

### Expected behavior
It should notice that it is a decorated function which modifies the return value of the function.


### pylint --version output
pylint 1.7.1, 
astroid 1.5.2
Python 3.4.3 (default, Nov 17 2016, 01:08:31) 
[GCC 4.8.4]

What about following code (based on [deckar01](https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/issues/259#issuecomment-267671718)'s above example) which gives false positive too-many-function-args error:
```python

    def wrapper(a, b, *args, **kwargs):
        print "helper wrapper: a={}".format(a)
        return fun(b, *args, **kwargs)
    return wrapper

@helper
def simple(b, c):
    print "simple: b={} c={}".format(b, c)

simple('argentina', 'brazil', 'china')
```
Its output is:

```
helper wrapper: a=argentina
simple: b=brazil c=china
```
And pylint  false positive error is:

issue.title: Added fast forward and rewind support to the Alexa cloud/smart home component

repository.name: core
repository.description: :house_with_garden: Open source home automation that puts local control and privacy first.

issue.body:
Added fast forward and rewind support to the Alexa cloud/smart home component.  It simply invokes the next and previous track functions.

## Description:
The Alexa PlaybackController interface supports fast forward and rewind, whereas Home Assistant's media_player component does not, only next_track and previous_track.  As a result, Alexa for the HA cloud skill or smart home skills does not support fast forward and rewind.

I propose adding fast forward and rewind and mapping them to next_track and previous_track, at least until Home Assistant's media_player ever gets fastforward and rewind services.  I've tested this on my local setup with success.  Existing users would probably have to rediscover their devices if they would want to make use of this functionality.

I'm not sure if I should add this capability to the docs [here](https://www.home-assistant.io/cloud/alexa/), since it might be confusing that media_player doesn't have those functions. Happy to add it if someone thinks I should.
